stories.summary: Draft PR #123 proposes an opt-in dispatcher with normal and historical modes, durable branch-backed handoffs, LFS hydration and verified checkpoint/push operations. It is not merged or approved for cutover; the existing dispatcher and claims remain unchanged.
stories.body: A newly surfaced draft pull request proposes a turn-scoped dispatcher that can resume work from branch-backed state and retire a checkout without force. Its normal and historical modes aim to reduce fragile handoffs while keeping the existing dispatcher untouched. The PR describes isolated Git tests and a design/cutover document, but explicitly requires review, full tests and an authorized cutover. Its branch is not evidence of a running service or accepted independent review. The separate private WIRE pointer is dated November 8 and too old for fresh operational counts.

sections.text: The proposal adds normal and historical modes, Git LFS asset hydration, verified checkpoints and pushes, and retirement that avoids forcing a checkout. These features target continuity and safer recovery when work spans several agent turns.

insights.explanation: Branch-backed continuity could make interrupted work easier to resume without relying on an agent's transient session state. That benefit is proposed, not yet demonstrated in production.

stories.headline: CUSTODIAN's ChatGPT relay moves to Firefox, then fixes message delivery and response polling
stories.summary: Two main-branch commits migrate CUSTODIAN's ChatGPT orchestration relay from Chrome to Firefox MCP and repair Send-button discovery, delivery confirmation and in-progress response detection. The follow-up reports 17 passing local tests and a reader smoke check; live unattended operation and independent acceptance remain unverified.
stories.body: The Firefox relay now connects Python scripts to an existing authenticated Firefox tab through Mozilla's DevTools MCP, without opening a browser or navigating to another conversation. A follow-up fixes selector drift that previously hid the enabled Send control, supports the current user-message marker to avoid false delivery timeouts, and detects response-starting state so the reader does not prematurely conclude that a reply is complete. The committed completion summary reports 17 unit tests passing, Python compilation, diff checks, a reader smoke test and a sender dry run. Those are reported local validations, not independent review or proof of an always-on host service. The separately published private WIRE pilot pointer was observed with a November 8 timestamp and is stale for current operational counts; none are imported.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN has rebuilt its ChatGPT conversation relay around Firefox and followed up with fixes for a fragile part of automated orchestration: knowing whether a message was actually sent and whether the reply has finished.

sections.heading: A different browser connection
sections.text: The Python sender and reader now connect to an existing Firefox session through Mozilla's DevTools MCP. They select the exact conversation instead of opening or navigating tabs, and keep browser lifetime separate from script lifetime.

sections.heading: The crucial fix is avoiding duplicate sends
sections.text: The follow-up targets a Send button missing from broad accessibility snapshots and a newer user-message marker that caused false delivery timeouts. The reader also recognizes a response that is starting but has not yet streamed. Together these changes make retry decisions safer, though they do not establish live reliability.

insights.title: Delivery confirmation matters more than clicking Send
insights.explanation: A false timeout can tempt an orchestrator to resend the same instruction. Checking the actual conversation before retrying reduces that duplicate-work risk.

insights.title: Tests are not service acceptance
insights.explanation: The commit records 17 passing local tests and a reader smoke check, but no independent acceptance or continuous-service proof. The next useful evidence is an end-to-end supervised run.

article.takeaway: The Firefox relay migration and scoped regression fixes are landed on main; their unattended operational reliability remains unverified.
article.next_watch: Watch for an independently evidenced exact-conversation send/poll cycle, supervised-service behavior, and any review receipt.

stories.body: A new main-branch commit adds a P0 agent-ops implementation packet and its independent review for a reported host-local Git reference obstruction. The packet cites host preflight reports of sixteen zero-byte loose remote-tracking refs, but those observations are not independently refreshed in this watch. The implementation must operate on an exact reviewed manifest, preserve private backups and unrelated Git state, default to dry-run, fail closed on races and mismatches, and prove rollback and dispatcher audit behavior. The paired review must independently validate host evidence and reject any damage to valid refs, worktrees or claims. Both packets carry ready/auto metadata, but their authoring text still says draft and not to auto-dispatch until approvals and claim checks complete. This documentation-versus-metadata discrepancy requires canonical dispatcher resolution, not an inferred claim. No code implementation, host mutation, independent PASS or verified teardown was observed. The separate WIRE pilot pointer remains stale; no private counts were imported.

stories.headline: Procgen ingress gets a coordinate fix for maps without a TileSet
stories.summary: A new main-branch change repairs tile/world coordinate conversions during TileSet-free procedural candidate evaluation and adds a focused regression test. A seed-123456 sandbox startup is reported, but broader validation remains unresolved due to LFS import and authored-level registry failures.
stories.body: Procedural generation can evaluate candidate layouts before a visual TileSet is populated. The ingress spawner now delegates tile-to-world mapping to the procgen tilemap's shared conversion contract, while reverse conversion uses the native 32-pixel structural grid when no TileSet is present. A focused regression covers positive, origin and negative tiles in both TileSet-free and TileSet-backed modes. The commit reports a user-confirmed manual seed-123456 sandbox startup, not independently verified full CI. Existing broader LFS import and authored-level registry failures still need follow-up. This landing does not prove independent acceptance, deployment or teardown.

stories.summary: A main-branch gameplay fix resets the reused camera's authored bounds when entering the Hub and adds a regression check for two Hub markers. This addresses a specific handoff bug, not a verified production deployment.
stories.body: The world transition manager now applies the destination map's camera bounds before rebinding the reused camera. article.lead: The journey from Awakening into the Hub now has a targeted camera fix on main. Previously, the camera could carry the previous area's boundaries into the next map, potentially constraining its view in the wrong place.

sections.heading: The destination takes control
sections.text: The transition manager now replaces the camera's authored bounds with the Hub map's bounds before completing the camera rebind. This makes the map handoff explicit rather than relying on retained camera state.

sections.heading: A regression check guards the handoff
sections.text: The smoke test verifies that both camera bound representations match the Hub and that two named destinations are inside them. The new assertions are visible in source; this watch did not execute the game.

insights.title: A reused camera needs new map authority
insights.explanation: Keeping the same camera object across scenes is efficient, but its old bounds must not survive a world transition. The fix targets that ownership boundary directly.

article.takeaway: The handoff fix and its regression assertions are landed, with runtime behavior still awaiting independent observation.
article.next_watch: Watch for passing Hub transition validation or a reproducible in-engine confirmation.

stories.headline: Operator chassis review gets a narrow source-scope repair, but acceptance remains gated
stories.summary: A correction for the Operator chassis-seal review has landed on main. It permits exactly one previously omitted test file only after the correction itself receives an authentic independent PASS. Focused and broader tests are reported passing, but the protected original review remains blocked and no recovery or cleanup is verified.
stories.body: The new source-scope attestation pins original source and archived packet identities, limiting the correction to one omitted lifecycle test file. The validator is designed to remain fail-closed until an independent accepted review of the correction is recorded. The implementation notes report four focused tests and a 300-test paired-review runner suite among broader passing checks. These are reported validations, not a new acceptance receipt. The protected original chassis review is still blocked; no host recovery, verdict or teardown is established.

article.lead: The blocked Operator chassis review now has a tightly scoped repair on main. Instead of bypassing the review system, the change documents one lifecycle test file that the original source declaration missed, then keeps the exception inactive until a separate reviewer accepts the correction.

sections.heading: A repair that does not waive review
sections.text: The attestation binds the original source archive, packet and code identities. Its validator rejects extra paths, changed source files and unapproved review states. The original chassis review stays blocked until the correction earns its own independent PASS.

sections.heading: Tests support the guard, not the final verdict
sections.text: Implementation notes report four focused tests and broader changed-file validation, including a 300-test review-runner suite. The watch did not rerun those tests, and no accepted correction receipt or original review verdict was inspected.

insights.title: The missing declaration was the bottleneck
insights.explanation: The review was stopped by an omitted lifecycle test in the declared source scope, not by permission to alter the original implementation. The correction targets that mismatch while retaining source identity checks.

insights.title: Approval is deliberately a separate switch
insights.explanation: Landing the correction does not activate the exception. Requiring a fresh independent PASS prevents a successful implementation commit from silently becoming review authority.

article.takeaway: The correction is published and narrowly bounded, but the original chassis review remains blocked until independently accepted correction evidence exists.
article.next_watch: Watch for an authentic independent PASS on the correction, followed by a fresh read-only recovery plan for the preserved chassis review.

stories.headline: Operator 3D animation gains an in-engine comparison preview, but production approval remains on hold
stories.summary: A focused Operator animation preview is now on main, allowing an unapproved 3D candidate to be compared against the accepted 2.5D source in Godot. The original batch-executor workstream is still incomplete, visual approval is absent, and a non-green lifecycle CI suite remains unresolved.
stories.body: Main commit dc48e1e9 adds a candidate-only Operator 3D preview scene and guarded request loader. The comparison pins the accepted 2.5D source and preserves the candidate_unapproved flag, with production approval and timing authority explicitly false. The commit reports baseline-equivalent authored-level CI errors documented in PR #119, but says the lifecycle suite remains non-green. Original executor ownership and remaining slices B–D are outstanding; independent paired acceptance and canonical teardown are not established.

article.lead: CUSTODIAN can now inspect a proposed 3D Operator animation inside Godot alongside the accepted 2.5D reference. That gives artists and gameplay reviewers a more useful comparison surface, but it is deliberately a preview, not permission to replace the playable character animation.

sections.heading: A safer place to judge the animation
sections.text: The new scene loads an explicitly unapproved candidate, checks its request digest and preserves a fixed reference to the accepted 2.5D artwork. Reviewers can compare the motion without granting production status or changing gameplay timing.

sections.heading: The larger animation pipeline is still unfinished
sections.text: This landing salvages only the first preview slice. Incremental batch execution, cache behavior and receipts remain unfinished. The original workstream is still open, and independent paired acceptance has not been established.

sections.heading: A test caveat still matters
sections.text: The commit cites independent review evidence that authored-level CI errors match the main baseline. That narrows one regression concern, but the lifecycle suite is still not green. A baseline comparison is not a passing test result.

insights.title: Baseline-equivalent failures are still failures

article.takeaway: The Operator 3D candidate is easier to evaluate, but remains unapproved and outside production animation authority.
article.next_watch: Watch for human visual comparison, completion of the remaining executor/cache slices, a resolved lifecycle suite and an independent acceptance receipt.

stories.headline: Awakening gains its first production score, with transition-safe music handoff
stories.summary: The approved 'A Command Still Speaking' cue is now integrated into Awakening's production scene. New ownership logic keeps music through the ten-part sequence and releases it on successful Hub transition, while preserving playback after a failed handoff. The author reports 35/35 changed-file validations and an independent code recheck, but audible listening and canonical teardown remain unverified.
stories.body: Main now contains the Awakening score, music director, two-deck ownership handling, a production handoff regression and a preserved validation archive. The author reports 35/35 changed-file tests passing, a graphical Godot boot, and a code reviewer rechecking the corrected real-transition smoke with no remaining findings. This is not a formal paired-review acceptance receipt, nor proof of audible loop quality. The cue's in-game seam and mixing still require human listening; host cleanup remains unknown.
bullets: Production scene now references the Awakening cue and dedicated music director.
Successful Hub handoff releases the cue; failed handoff retains ownership.
Author-reported 35/35 validations and independent code recheck are not formal acceptance.

article.lead: Awakening now has a production music cue. 'A Command Still Speaking' is wired into the opening sequence with rules that keep the score playing across scene beats and release it cleanly when the player reaches the Hub. The change reaches beyond adding an audio file: it handles failed transitions without abruptly losing the music.

sections.heading: Music that follows the scene, not the loading screen
sections.text: A dedicated director uses the existing two-deck music manager. It keeps the score through ten Awakening sections and optional Chapel content. On a successful Hub handoff, the cue fades without bringing back the prior playlist; a failed transition keeps the cue under Awakening's ownership.

sections.heading: Tests cover the real transition
sections.text: The first focused test did not exercise the production handoff path. After an independent code-review finding, the author added a regression that runs the actual transition and rollback behavior. The implementation summary reports 35 passing changed-file validations and a successful graphical startup, but no audible playback check.

insights.title: The transition boundary was the real risk
insights.explanation: The important fix is not just starting music, but preventing a successful transition from restoring an unwanted playlist and a failed transition from silencing the scene. The new regression targets that behavior.

insights.title: Green audio tests cannot certify the listening experience
insights.explanation: Technical validation supports scene integration and ownership behavior. It cannot establish whether the loop seam is audible or the mix feels right during gameplay; that remains a human audition.

article.takeaway: The Awakening score is integrated on main with meaningful regression coverage, while listening approval and verified host closeout remain separate gates.
article.next_watch: Look for a human in-game listening check, a formal finish receipt if applicable, and trustworthy canonical cleanup evidence.
